thesis: Every one of these eight signals (AgentBench, MAST taxonomies, pass@k reliability science, Diagrid verifiable execution, OWASP APTS safety controls, recover-bench, tool-to-agent retrieval, operator-runtime commentary) is converging on free, incumbent-supplied agent evaluation and runtime assurance, so the only asset a governed function can still own is its own audited before/after record of false closes, review load, and recoveries on real commitments; the deferred, untested commercial hypothesis remains that a buyer prices a governed function by that record before inspecting its harness, and it stays unactionable until Shadow's live commitment-to-closure function can produce the record, which this sandbox (no git repository, three stale post JSON files) cannot verify.
doctrine: When a research signal names a verifier, benchmark, taxonomy, or runtime control that an incumbent ships for free, Shadow adopts or ignores it but never rebuilds it; a signal earns code only when it maps to a demonstrated failure in the live function's own outcome ledger, and the frontier compound loop records 'no decision changed' rather than manufacturing wiring when it runs outside the repository.
